Priya to share initial sizing + HW recommendations for 100 RPS pilot (by 2026-11-06)

summary: Discovery call focused on Marlow Health's requirements for an on-prem, air-gapped deployment of Redwood for PHI workloads. Key concerns: offline updates, hardware constraints, vendor approval, encryption/KMS, audit logs, and timelines. Redwood AE + SE explained Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private options and proposed pilot approach. Agreed next steps: share security artifacts, sizing, and schedule deep technical session.
topics: Air-gapped update process and signed bundles
Hardware sizing and GPU availability (A100 vs A30/V100)
Fallbacks to hosted for non-PHI data
questions: How will updates be delivered in an air-gapped environment?
Can Redwood support our current cluster with mix of A100 and older GPUs?
What audit/logging guarantees are available (retention, tamper-evidence)?
Can we run inference without any outbound internet connectivity?
transcript:
[00:00] Jordan Ellis: Hey everyone, thanks for joining—I'm Jordan from Redwood, AE on this account. Priya's my SE, she'll take the deep infra bits. Quick roll call?
[00:08] Dr. Evan Ross: Evan Ross here, CTO at Marlow Health.
[00:11] Maya Lin: Maya Lin, Head of Cloud Ops.
[00:14] Carlos Vega: Carlos, Security Architect.
[00:16] Samantha Price: Sam from Product.
[00:18] Ben Hart: Ben, DevOps.
[00:22] Jordan Ellis: Great. Agenda is to understand your requirements for on-prem and specifically air-gapped PHI workloads, constraints, and success criteria. We'll cover update model, networking, hardware, and timeline.
[00:34] Priya Kapoor: Hi all. We'll try to be pragmatic—what works in your environment and where we can be flexible.
[00:40] Maya Lin: Cool. To start, we process a lot of PHI. Our security and legal teams mandate no egress of PHI, and most of the inference must run in our secure data centers. We need an air-gapped option for the model serving.
[00:54] Jordan Ellis: Understood. To confirm, you want a fully offline deployment, or is a controlled, one-way outbound allowed for signed update pulls?
[01:02] Carlos Vega: Prefer fully air-gapped. Any outbound is a huge policy lift. But we are open to approved USB/hard-media signed bundles if that's standard.
[01:11] Priya Kapoor: That's something we've done with other customers—signed artifact bundles, checksums and signatures, and an offline installer. We also support an appliance-style deployment where the control plane is customer-hosted.
[01:22] Ben Hart: Quick Q: What do you mean by 'appliance'? VM images? Containers?
[01:26] Priya Kapoor: We provide containerized images and an orchestration recipe. For air-gap setups we hand off a signed tarball with images and a verifiable manifest. There is a small local control plane that runs metrics, routing, and the model runtime.
[01:38] Samantha Price: Do you have docs? Our procurement needs vendor packaging details.
[01:42] Jordan Ellis: Yes, we'll share the air-gap playbook and network diagram.
[01:45] Dr. Evan Ross: Our hardware story—most of our racks are 2x A100, but some older hosts still have V100s and a couple of A30s. We can't buy a brand new cluster immediately, budget cycle later. Can Redwood run on mixed hardware?
[01:58] Priya Kapoor: Short answer: yes, but performance differs. We can target quantized models and smaller model variants on older GPUs. For consistent latency we'd recommend standardizing, but for pilot it's common to use mixed infra. We'll include a compatibility matrix in the sizing doc.
[02:12] Maya Lin: Also interested in model sizes. Our use is mostly structured note summarization and triage—so likely a 7B-13B class model would be fine if it meets quality. Do you support custom fine-tuning?
[02:23] Jordan Ellis: We support running both open and customer-fine-tuned models; for private deployments you bring your model artifact or we can help with onboarding. Fine-tuning may change resource requirements.
[02:31] Carlos Vega: Security: KMS is big for us. Keys must remain on-prem in an HSM and we need key rotation policies and auditable logs. Does Redwood integrate with customer KMS/HSM?
[02:41] Priya Kapoor: Yes we integrate with customer-managed KMS/HSM. On private deployments the decrypting keys can stay in your HSM; the local runtime requests keys via a connector which can be configured in air-gap mode using a local key proxy. We'll provide reference architecture.
[02:55] Ben Hart: How about patching and updates? We can't have random background downloads.
[02:58] Priya Kapoor: For air-gapped, updates are manual: you pull a signed bundle, validate signatures, and apply. Patches to the runtime are in those bundles. We also provide a rollout utility that simulates canaries locally.
[03:10] Samantha Price: Any experience with regulatory audits? We'll need evidence for HIPAA and SOC2.
[03:14] Jordan Ellis: We have other healthcare customers—can share SOC2, and ISO certs as applicable, plus audit logs. We'll include sample audit output showing access logs, model versions, and who triggered deploys.
[03:26] Carlos Vega: Are logs tamper-evident? We use a SIEM and need a signed chain or at least append-only logs with integrity checks.
[03:34] Priya Kapoor: We can emit signed audit events, and we've integrated with Splunk/ELK/Syslog. The air-gapped mode writes to local log stores which you can forward to your SIEM via approved connectors.
[03:46] Dr. Evan Ross: Latency and throughput: our triage flow needs p95 latency under 350ms for short prompts, and sustained throughput about 100 RPS. Is that realistic on 2x A100 hosts?
[03:58] Priya Kapoor: 350ms p95 is tight but doable with optimized runtime, batching disabled for latency-critical routes, and KV cache priming. 100 RPS will need concurrency and likely multiple worker pods. We'll size that in the doc. For older GPUs, those numbers will degrade.
[04:14] Ben Hart: What's your runtime's memory/disk footprint? We have limited local NVMe across nodes.
[04:18] Priya Kapoor: For a 13B FP16 model you'd be looking at ~40-60GB GPU memory depending on quantization; disk for model weights ~50-70GB. We'll provide detailed breakdowns.
[04:30] Maya Lin: Dependency constraints: our change control only allows approved vendor software. Are you able to produce SBOMs?
[04:36] Jordan Ellis: Yes, we'll produce an SBOM and list of all packages in the runtime.
[04:40] Samantha Price: On fallback: if a model needs to call a hosted tool for heavy-lift tasks, does that break PHI policies? We might want dual-path where PHI stays local but deidentified traffic could go to hosted.
[04:52] Priya Kapoor: You can partition by route: keep PHI-bound routes local and non-PHI to hosted. We support routing policies that can be static based on endpoint, or dynamic with a policy engine. For SOS we can also offer token redaction at the edge.
[05:06] Carlos Vega: What about key escrow and emergency access? Our legal team wants time-limited emergency access via multi-party approval.
[05:12] Jordan Ellis: We can support an emergency access workflow that requires multiple approvers; we'll work with your security org to define the SOP.
[05:20] Dr. Evan Ross: Timeline question—if we want a proof-of-concept, what do you recommend?
[05:24] Priya Kapoor: Typical path: 2-week discovery + agreement, then 4-8 week pilot to run traffic on a small subset (1-3 nodes), then expansion. For air-gapped it's often 6-10 weeks due to procurement and approvals.
[05:36] Maya Lin: Procurement: we have a vendor onboarding checklist—insurance, SOC2, SLAs. Can you provide references?
[05:42] Jordan Ellis: Yes, we'll provide references and our standard onboarding package.
[05:47] Ben Hart: Quick technical: KV cache—how is that persisted across restarts in air-gapped mode?
[05:52] Priya Kapoor: KV cache can be persisted to local encrypted disk. If you have distributed cache restrictions, we can configure sticky routing so that session affinity keeps cache warm on a node.
[06:04] Samantha Price: Any known issues around GPU scheduling when mixing old and new cards?
[06:08] Priya Kapoor: Scheduler needs to be aware of device types; we'll supply node labels and a scheduler config. For mixed deployments you'll see variability; again pilot for validation is standard.
[06:20] Jordan Ellis: Pricing callout—air-gapped + private is a different packaging than hosted; there are setup fees and per-node licensing. We'll put numbers in the pricing doc.
[06:30] Dr. Evan Ross: One more: how do you handle model provenance—who changed model weights, when, and why? We need traceability.
[06:36] Priya Kapoor: We track model artifacts with checksums, version IDs, and a deployment audit log with user IDs. That will all be in the audit output.
[06:46] Carlos Vega: Do you support hardware HSM integration for signing images on our side?
[06:50] Priya Kapoor: Yes. We can accept images signed by your HSM and verify signature during install.
[06:56] Maya Lin: Any limitations on supported OS or container runtimes? We run a hardened RHEL variant and containerd.
[07:02] Priya Kapoor: We support RHEL and Ubuntu LTS; containerd is supported—the install docs will include recommended kernel and cgroups settings.
[07:12] Jordan Ellis: Okay, sounds like we have enough to put together the artifacts. Quick recap?
[07:16] Dr. Evan Ross: Recap from our side—fully air-gapped deployment requirement, mixed GPU estate today, need HSM/KMS on-prem integration, SBOM/SOC2 evidence, and a pilot timeline aiming for Jan production depending on approvals.
[07:28] Jordan Ellis: From Redwood: we'll send SOC2 and air-gap playbook, Priya will prepare sizing for 100 RPS and hardware compatibility, and we'll propose pilot pricing and timelines.
[07:36] Samantha Price: Also please include a sample contract addendum for on-prem licensing and support SLAs.
[07:40] Jordan Ellis: Will do.
[07:42] Ben Hart: I might reach out to Priya offline about node labeling and some of our IaC templates.
[07:46] Priya Kapoor: Happy to do that.
[07:49] Jordan Ellis: Great—thanks everyone. We'll follow up with the docs and get that deep-dive scheduled.
[07:54] Dr. Evan Ross: Thanks all.
[07:56] (call ends)

Notes on transcription: occasional mis-hearings and filler removed for clarity; some product names abbreviated.
